questions.prompt: Studies suggest many Indian school children are short-sighted and need spectacles, but some never get them. Explain what kind of lens corrects short sight, and suggest how schools could help.
questions.modelAnswer: A short-sighted eye focuses light from distant objects in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the light slightly before it enters the eye, so it focuses on the retina and distant things look sharp. Schools could organise free eye tests, provide low-cost spectacles, sit affected children closer to the board, encourage outdoor play (linked to less short-sightedness) and reduce the stigma of wearing glasses.
rubric: Explains it moves the focus back onto the retina
At least two sensible school actions
